target.title: fix(read): normalize displayed line ranges for limits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the session read tool call display could show misleading line ranges when a caller supplied a non-positive, fractional, or non-finite `limit`, even though the read execution path normalizes those limits before slicing file content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The expanded read call renderer now applies the same positive-limit normalization used by the read execution path before computing the displayed line range. This stays inside the session read tool owner boundary, leaves offset validation and tool schemas unchanged, and does not add compatibility, config, provider, or public API behavior.

## User Impact

Users reviewing read tool activity see line ranges that match the page the tool will actually read, instead of raw numeric input such as `:1-0`, `:1-1.5`, or `:1-Infinity`.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: expanded read call rendering normalizes displayed line ranges for non-positive, fractional, and non-finite `limit` values using the same positive-limit contract as read execution.
- Current-head real behavior proof at `048fc1bcceb7faf3a339cc2ae148a602c56fb7d0`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module --eval "import { createReadToolDefinition } from './src/agents/sessions/tools/read.ts'; const theme = { fg: (_token, text) => text, bold: (text) => text }; const tool = createReadToolDefinition(process.cwd()); const cases = [['limit=-1', { path: 'notes.txt', limit: -1 }], ['limit=1.5', { path: 'notes.txt', limit: 1.5 }], ['limit=Infinity', { path: 'notes.txt', limit: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY }]]; for (const [label, args] of cases) { const component = tool.renderCall(args, theme, { lastComponent: undefined, expanded: true, cwd: process.cwd() }); console.log(label + ' -> ' + component.render(120).join('\n').trimEnd()); }"` passed by loading the production `createReadToolDefinition(...).renderCall` hook and rendering expanded read calls.

  Copied runtime output:

  ```text
  limit=-1 -> read notes.txt:1-1
  limit=1.5 -> read notes.txt:1-1
  limit=Infinity -> read notes.txt:1-2000
  ```

- Focused regression proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts` passed with 14 tests passing.
- PR diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit ad39fefa776d7c07dc397eb32e136c7efcdc981a --model gpt-5.6-terra` passed with no accepted/actionable findings for the patch commit.
- Observed result: the real renderer and focused regression both display `read notes.txt:1-1` for `limit=-1` and `limit=1.5`, and `read notes.txt:1-2000` for `limit=Infinity`, matching the execution-side limit normalization.
